terra.problem: Saying the list got bigger treats the sanctified ones and the warriors as separate groups. The verse does not say they are separate.
The oven-mitt joke has no clear connection to the warriors being summoned, and losing arguments to oven mitts does not make sense.
Calling the warriors the second group assumes they are distinct from the sanctified ones. The verse does not make that distinction.
The chocolate-chip joke plays on literal melting rather than the fear described in the passage. The comparison does not share the action of the Bible picture.
Pride is not named twice in the verse. It names the haughtiness of the arrogant and the pride of the ruthless.
Saying treasure is not what draws the Medes extends the verse beyond their lack of regard for silver and desire for gold, and implies a reason for their actions.
The casserole joke mentions a food outside the passage, breaking the food rule.
